subject: general
question: A sector of a circle with a radius of 15 cm has a central angle of 45°. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of π/4 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For sectors of the same circle, the area is directly proportional to the central angle.

Angle of the first sector = 45°

Angle of the second sector = π/4 radians = (180° ÷ 4) = 45°

Since both central angles are equal, their areas will be exactly the same.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 15 cm

Central angle of first sector (θ₁) = 45°

Central angle of second sector (θ₂) = π/4 radians

 
 

 

 45°
 r = 15 cm
 First Sector
 
 
 

 

 π/4
 r = 15 cm
 Second Sector
 
 
 Ratio = ?

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector (when θ is in degrees) = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Area of a sector (when θ is in radians) = (1 ÷ 2) × r²θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of first sector = (45° ÷ 360°) × π × (15)²

⇒ Area of first sector = (1 ÷ 8) × 225π = 28.125π cm²

⇒ Area of second sector = (1 ÷ 2) × (15)² × (π ÷ 4)

⇒ Area of second sector = (1 ÷ 2) × 225 × (π ÷ 4) = 28.125π cm²

⇒ Ratio of areas = Area of first sector : Area of second sector

⇒ Ratio = 28.125π : 28.125π = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × πr² if θ is measured in degrees, and (1 ÷ 2)r²θ if θ is measured in radians.

Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert an angle from radians into degrees, multiply the radian value by (180° ÷ π). For example, π radians equals 180°.

Length of an Arc

The arc length of a corresponding sector is calculated as (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr (for degrees) or simply rθ (for radians).
